question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x({y}^{2}-1)}{{y}^{2}(x+3)}, & x\ge 0,\,y\ge 1 \\ 0, & x<0\,\text{or}\,y<1.\end{aligned}
$$

Find ${F}_{X}(x),$ the marginal CDF of $X,$ for $x\ge 1.$
question.worked_solution:
The marginal CDF of $X$ is given by

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=F(x,\infty )={lim}_{y\to \infty }F(x,y).
$$

Therefore, for $x\ge 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{X}(x) & ={lim}_{y\to \infty }(\frac{x({y}^{2}-1)}{{y}^{2}(x+3)}) \\  & =\frac{x}{x+3}{lim}_{y\to \infty }(\frac{{y}^{2}-1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{x}{x+3}{lim}_{y\to \infty }(1-\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{x}{x+3}{lim}_{y\to \infty }(1-0) \\  & =\frac{x}{x+3}.\end{aligned}
$$
